question:
A customer wants to remove the option to override the renewal term during an asset renewal process initiated from the Account > Managed Assets view.
How should a Revenue Cloud Consultant fulfill this requirement?
optionA: Modify the Lightning web component corresponding to the renew assets page and remove the option for early renewal.
optionB: Modify the flow Amend, Renew, and Cancel Assets screen component for renewal term and remove the option for early renewal.
optionC: Modify the flow Renew Assets screen component for renewal term and remove the option for early renewal.
explanation:
Modifying the Amend, Renew, and Cancel Assets flow's screen component for renewal term is how the consultant removes the option. Renewal from Account > Managed Assets runs through one screen flow, and Salesforce names it: Set Up Asset Lifecycle Flows says to open Revenue Settings, find Set Up Flow for Managing Assets, and "Enter the name of the Amend, Renew, and Cancel Salesforce Flow for the system to use when users select the Amend, Renew, or Cancel buttons in the Managed Assets Viewer"; Enabling Revenue Settings gives its default API name as runtime_revenue_arcflows__arcFlow and says "To use a custom flow, enter the API name of the flow that you created." The Set Renewal Term screen with its Override Renewal Term option is a screen in that flow. Removing the option means cloning the Amend, Renew, and Cancel flow, editing the renewal-term screen component, and registering the custom flow's API name in Revenue Settings.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the renew assets Lightning web component) — the components behind these screens are not a supported customization point; the documented extension mechanism is the flow whose API name Revenue Settings holds, the same pattern used for the quote-to-contract and quote-to-order flows.
Option C (a Renew Assets flow) — no separately registered "Renew Assets" flow is documented; the amend, renew and cancel actions share the single flow named above.

corrected.note: Key moved C to B. The 2026-08-15 pass could not confirm the flow name and kept C. Set Up Asset Lifecycle Flows documents a single "Amend, Renew, and Cancel Salesforce Flow" registered under Set Up Flow for Managing Assets (default runtime_revenue_arcflows__arcFlow), and no standalone Renew Assets flow appears anywhere in the Revenue Management documentation; the deck's own items on this flow (1092afe5, c60cb035) already treat it as the amend, renew, and cancel flow. The predefined flow could still contain a subflow of that name inside the managed package, which the documentation does not show, so this is a judgment call the owner may reverse.

question:
A law firm is using Revenue Cloud's Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) capability. The law firm creates very large Merger & Acquisitions (M&A) contracts for its commercial customers. The contract designer sets a requirement to structure and organize the content more effectively. This will help the contract designer quickly navigate the document and include the appropriate clauses, tables, and contract text in the document.
How should a template designer meet this requirement?
optionA: Create a structure in a document template.
optionB: Create child templates under the main document template.
optionC: Create a section in a document template.
explanation:
Creating a section in the document template is how the template designer meets the requirement. Sections are the structural unit of a document template: Create Section in Document Template says the designer "can define sections within the document to structure and organize the content more effectively" — in the Microsoft 365 editor, from the Salesforce Contracts for Word add-in, Insert New | Section, name and describe it, and save — and states the payoff in the stem's own words: "Contract designers can quickly navigate to specific sections and include the appropriate clauses, tables, and contract text within each section."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (create a structure) — not a template feature; structure is the result of adding sections.
Option B (child templates under the main template) — would fragment the agreement into separate documents rather than organise one long one.

question:
An IT service provider purchased Revenue Cloud. Currently, the provider needs to mark its Super Duper Product as an automatically renewable product with no manual interaction from users.
How should a Revenue Cloud Consultant handle this requirement?
optionA: Select the Auto Renew checkbox on the product selling model.
optionB: Select the Auto Renew checkbox on the Asset object.
optionC: Select the Auto Renew checkbox on the Product2 object.
explanation:
Selecting the Auto Renew checkbox on the product selling model is how the consultant marks the product as automatically renewable. The product-level default lives on the product selling model: the Summer '25 release note "Simplify Transaction Management with Auto-Renewals for Term Based Products" gives the procedure in one line — "Open a term based product selling model, click Edit, and then select Automatically Renew Asset by Default." Products configured that way default to auto-renewal when an order is assetized, and the Automatically Renew Expiring Assets flow template then creates and activates renewal orders for assets that are expiring and marked for automatic renewal. The Asset Renewal Automation Templates article lists the fields to expose: "Show the Automatically Renew Asset by Default field on Product Selling Model pages" and "Show the Automatically Renew field on Quote Line Item, Order Item, and Asset pages."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (the checkbox on the Asset object) — an Automatically Renew field does exist on the Asset, but it marks one customer's asset and is the per-deal override that "sales reps can then override" on individual orders; the requirement is to mark the product itself, which is the selling-model default.
Option C (the checkbox on Product2) — Product2 carries no auto-renew field; renewal behaviour is a property of how the product is sold — its term-defined selling model — not of the product record.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ind.qocal_manage_assets_in_revenue_lifecycle_management.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Key moved B to A. A 2026-08-04 comment moved this C to B on the (correct) ground that Product2 has no Auto Renew field, but the product-level setting is documented on the Product Selling Model: the Summer '25 release note reads "Open a term based product selling model, click Edit, and then select Automatically Renew Asset by Default", and the flow-template article lists that field on Product Selling Model pages with a separate per-asset Automatically Renew field on Quote Line Item, Order Item, and Asset. The Asset field is the per-deal override, not the product default.

question:
A Cloud Consultant is using Contracts AI to retrieve clauses and contract fields from a PDF. After the initial run, the consultant realizes that a payment method custom field needs to be retrieved that was not initially included.

What should the consultant do to retrieve this custom field?
optionA: Modify the contract extraction template to define the attribute mapping and context mapping for payment method.
optionB: Modify the AI prompt template to define the attribute mapping and context mapping for payment method.
optionC: Log a support case with Salesforce to enable payment method to be added to the extraction mapping used.
explanation:
Modifying the contract extraction template to define the attribute mapping and context mapping for payment method is what the consultant should do. Attribute mapping and context mapping live on the contract extraction template, not on an AI prompt template: the documentation says you create the extraction template to define the attribute mapping, context mapping, and prompt instructions that generative AI uses to extract contract details from a file. Within that flow, clicking Create Attribute Definition clones the standard ContractsExtractionContext context definition, and user-defined fields are then added as attributes and mapped to the corresponding contract fields. So retrieving a field missed on the first run means going back into the extraction template — Edit, then Add Attributes, specifying attribute name, type, and data type, then mapping the new field to the contract field.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (modify the AI prompt template) — the prompt template shapes the instructions given to the model; it is not where field-level attribute and context mapping is configured.
Option C (log a support case) — unnecessary; this is self-service admin configuration.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ind.sf_contracts_create_a_contract_extraction_template_for_extraction.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ind.sf_contracts_View_the_Standard_ContractsExtractionContext_Mapping.htm&language=en_US&type=5

Attribute mapping and context mapping are documented as living on the contract extraction template — the template is defined as the thing that holds them — so 'Modify the AI prompt template' was wrong. question: Universal Containers is expanding into French- and German-speaking regions. The team wants to ensure that product names and descriptions appear in the correct language when customers browse the catalog via APIs.
optionA: Use data translation via Translation Workbench to modify the metadata API and Product List API.
optionB: Provide data translations using standard Salesforce Product2 APIs and Product Details API.
optionC: Enable data translation and provide values via the Product List API and Product Details API.
explanation:
Enabling data translation and providing values via the Product List API and Product Details API is the approach. Translate Product Catalog Data explains that PCM otherwise shows product and catalog data only in the org's base language, and that data translation "lets admins add translated values for products, categories, and attributes. At runtime, users see product names, descriptions, and filters in their configured language." Product2 Name, Description, Help Text and picklist values are translatable, translations are added in bulk through STF or XLIFF files or manually on the Translations tab, and they appear only after Use Indexed Data for Product Listing and Search is on and a full reindex has run.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Translation Workbench modifying the Metadata API and Product List API) — Translation Workbench is where metadata labels are translated; product data translation is a PCM feature with its own setup, and the Metadata API is not involved in serving catalog data.
Option B (standard Product2 APIs and Product Details API) — standard Product2 APIs return the base-language record; the localised experience is delivered by the Product Discovery APIs after data translation is enabled.

question:
A sales user is trying to add products to a Quote using Product Discovery via Browse Catalog in Revenue Cloud. However, they are unable to see the products they are looking to add.

What is the reason for this issue?
optionA: The products are not associated with an active price book entry that belongs to the price book selected on the Quote.
optionB: The sales user profile does not have the "View All" on Product2 object permission, allowing users to have access to all the Products.
optionC: The Product Discovery component on the Quote Layout is misconfigured or hidden and unable to be accessed on Lightning page.
explanation:
The products not being associated with an active price book entry in the price book selected on the Quote is the reason. Browse Catalog only offers products the quote can price: the Products List (POST) resource behind it takes priceBookId as a required property — prices come from the standard price book if none is given — and with Price Book Filtering turned on in Product Discovery Settings it "retrieves only the products that are associated with the selected price book". A product without an active price book entry in the quote's price book therefore either does not appear or cannot be priced and added.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (no View All on Product2) — object-level visibility; Product Discovery users see products through the Product Catalog Management Viewer permission set, and a missing View All would not explain some products being absent while others show.
Option C (the Product Discovery component is misconfigured or hidden) — if the component were missing, the user could not browse at all, rather than browse and find specific products missing.

question:
A company's IT team is planning to implement Revenue Cloud. Their team consists of business analysts and administrators. The company plans to solve a complex and major use case of omni-channel selling, allowing its customers to buy directly from its third-party website as well as via its sales reps. The company also plans to hire new staff to support this project.

Which skill set does the IT team need to successfully implement this project?
optionA: Expertise in Salesforce Integration, including REST APIs
optionB: Expertise in Salesforce flows
optionC: Expertise in Apex and Lightning Web Component development
explanation:
Expertise in Salesforce integration, including REST APIs, is the skill set the IT team needs. Omni-channel selling through a third-party website means the external channel has to call into Revenue Cloud — Product Discovery for browsing and Place Sales Transaction for orders are REST APIs — so connecting the website to Salesforce is integration work, and it is the one skill a team of analysts and administrators does not already have.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Salesforce flows) — a skill the administrators already bring, and flows do not connect a third-party website to Salesforce.
Option C (Apex and Lightning Web Component development) — useful for customising the in-org experience, but the use case is an external channel calling the platform's APIs, not custom UI or Apex.

question:
A large enterprise customer, Universal Containers (UC), has negotiated a special, long-term agreement with a software vendor for its enterprise-wide licensing. This agreement includes custom pricing tiers, specific discounts that apply only to UC across various product families, and unique billing frequencies tied to UC's fiscal year. The sales team needs to ensure that all future quotes and orders for UC automatically reflect these pre-negotiated terms.

How should the sales team consistently apply these specific pricing and billing conditions for UC?
optionA: Use Discount Schedules on relevant products, with a Price Rule that applies these custom schedules only when UC is the designated account.
optionB: Establish a dedicated price book for UC that is populated with UC's negotiated prices, and includes all custom rates and specific billing rules for its products.
optionC: Create a Contracted Pricing record on the contract associated with the UC Account that details product-specific prices, tiered discounts, and special billing arrangements.
explanation:
Creating a Contracted Pricing record on the contract associated with the UC Account, detailing product-specific prices, tiered discounts and special billing arrangements, is how the sales team applies the negotiated terms consistently. Contracted Pricing stores account-specific negotiated pricing and terms against the contract, so future quotes and orders for that account automatically pick those conditions up without the rep re-entering them.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Discount Schedules with a Price Rule keyed on the account) — Salesforce CPQ constructs, not Revenue Cloud's pricing model, and they express discounts rather than a negotiated agreement with billing terms.
Option B (a dedicated price book for UC) — a price book carries list prices per product; it cannot hold tiered discounts across product families or billing frequencies, and it has to be maintained separately from the contract that governs the deal.

question: A Billing Operations user at Universal Containers is configuring a new order for a software subscription product that starts on July 1. This product is assigned a Billing Treatment at the Product Level that bills in arrears. However, the Billing Treatment assigned at the Order Product level is configured to bill in advance. What is the correct statement regarding Billing Treatment?
optionA: Billing Treatment resolution always prefers the Product Level over the Order Product level.
optionB: Billing Treatment at the Order Product level overrides the Product Level Billing Treatment.
optionC: Billing Treatments are only evaluated when no Legal Entity is defined.
explanation:
Billing Treatment at the Order Product level overrides the Product Level Billing Treatment — that is the correct statement. The more specific assignment wins, so this subscription bills in advance. A billing treatment item is where the detail of when and how a customer is billed for an order product is set, and resolving from the order product outward is what allows a single catalog product to be sold on different billing terms in different deals without cloning the product.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Product level always preferred) — inverts the resolution, which would make an order-level treatment unusable.
Option C (only evaluated when no Legal Entity is defined) — the legal entity carries accounting and regional configuration; it does not gate whether billing treatments apply.

question:
A company creates large quotes with hundreds of line items. These line items need to be exported in a specific format.

What should the sales reps use to generate these line items in the required format?
optionA: Document Builder
optionB: Custom Report
optionC: OmniStudio Document Generation
explanation:
OmniStudio Document Generation is what the exam keys for generating hundreds of line items in a required format. It is the engine Salesforce documents for large, format-controlled transaction documents: Generate Documents for Large Transactions covers "high-volume transactions, such as large telecom invoices, manufacturing quotes, and insurance schedules", using Context Service token mapping and Data Processing Engine transforms, and its limits table puts standard processing at up to 1,000 transaction lines and large processing at up to 15,000. Because the output is a designer-built template, the line items come out in whatever layout the required format demands rather than in a fixed grid.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Document Builder) — a real quote-document feature in Revenue Management — turned on in Revenue Settings, it builds "professional, customized, and dynamic quote documents" from drag-in components such as Grid — and the simpler tool for an ordinary quote PDF. The exam keys OmniStudio for this scenario on the volume-and-format wording; on a current org both tools can produce a quote document, so this item has two defensible options.
Option B (Custom Report) — lists the line items but gives no control over document layout, so it cannot satisfy a format specification.

question: A smartphone product is currently sold as a one-time upfront payment. In order for it to be sold with equal monthly installment payments for 12 months, what should the consultant set up?
optionA: Assign a product selling model option of Term Annual to the product.
optionB: Assign a product selling model option of Term Monthly to the product.
optionC: Assign a product selling model option of Evergreen Monthly to the product.
explanation:
Assigning a product selling model option of Term Monthly to the product is the setup. Equal monthly installments over twelve months are a term-defined selling model with a monthly pricing term. A product selling model has a selling model type (one-time, term-defined or evergreen) and, for term-defined and evergreen models, a pricing term and unit that set how the price is expressed and billed; assigning a Term Monthly model to the smartphone makes it a 12-month subscription priced per month, alongside or instead of the one-time model it has today.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Term Annual) — prices the term per year, so the customer would be charged once a year rather than in twelve equal monthly payments.
Option C (Evergreen Monthly) — bills monthly but has no fixed term; it renews indefinitely until cancelled, which does not match a 12-month installment plan.

question:
A sales rep needs to renew multiple assets. Some assets will be renewed at the same prices, so negotiations are unnecessary and the rep can directly create a renewal order. Some assets need to be renewed at higher prices, so the rep needs to create a quote for negotiation. When the sales rep starts the renewal process, they are not able to choose whether to create a quote or an order.

How should a Revenue Cloud Consultant address the sales rep's issue?
optionA: Customize the Manage Asset component to allow renewal quote and order creation.
optionB: Override the standard Salesforce flow to allow renewal quote and order creation.
optionC: Change the Revenue Cloud settings to allow renewal quote and order creation.
explanation:
Overriding the standard Salesforce flow to allow renewal quote and order creation is how the consultant addresses it. The amend, renew, and cancel experience is a screen flow, and Revenue Settings only names which flow runs — it carries no switch that adds a quote-or-order choice. Setup > Revenue Settings > Set Up Flow for Managing Assets takes "the API name of the screen flow that will be used when amending, renewing, and canceling assets", defaulting to the predefined runtime_revenue_arcflows__arcFlow, and the documented way to change what that experience offers is the next sentence: "To use a custom flow, enter the API name of the flow that you created."
One caveat worth carrying into the exam: the documentation never states outright that the predefined flow withholds the choice. The stem asserts it, and given that, the flow is the only documented place the behaviour can change.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (customise the Manage Asset component) — the wrong layer: the component launches the flow, it does not define what the flow offers.
Option C (change Revenue Cloud settings) — the settings that page documents are Enable Revenue Cloud Features, Create Application Usage Type, the three flow API names, and Configure Products at Runtime — none of them a renewal quote-versus-order toggle.

question: For Lot-based or As-Is Renewals, how should a user trace an Asset's renewal price breakdown back to its original Net Unit Price?
optionA: Review the Asset's Asset State Period record(s).
optionB: Review the Asset's Asset Action Source record(s).
optionC: Review Asset's Asset Action record(s).
explanation:
Reviewing the Asset's Asset Action Source records is how a user traces a renewal price back to its original Net Unit Price. Asset Action Source records carry the prices of each prior transaction: the developer guide describes the object as "an optional way to record what transactions caused changes to lifecycle-managed assets. Use it to trace financial and other information about asset actions", and its fields include ListPrice, UnitPrice, NetUnitPrice, Quantity, StartDate, EndDate and the reference to the order product. A lot-based renewal honours each lot at its original purchase price, so the breakdown on the renewal quote line details traces back to those records — one per prior sale or amendment.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Asset State Period records) — hold quantity, amount and MRR for a span of time; they do not record which transaction set the price or that transaction's net unit price.
Option C (Asset Action records) — record that a change happened and its category (new sale, upsell, renewal), with the quantity, amount and MRR change; the transaction-level price detail lives on the source records.

question: A project is moving from the design phase to the build phase. What should a Revenue Cloud Consultant do to ensure a successful build cycle?
optionA: Set up environments for development, testing, and production, and choose a deployment tool.
optionB: Write user stories, have user workshops to confirm requirements, and build test use cases.
optionC: Build in the production environment, let users test it live, and provide feedback in real time.
explanation:
Setting up environments for development, testing and production, and choosing a deployment tool, is what makes a build cycle succeed. Building needs somewhere to build that is not production, somewhere to test that is not the build org, and a defined way to promote metadata between them; without those in place before development starts, every change is either made live or has no path to go live.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (user stories, workshops, test cases) — design-phase work; the project is leaving design, and requirements should already be confirmed.
Option C (build in production with live user testing) — puts untested configuration in front of real transactions and gives no way to roll a change back.

question:
Universal Containers sells customizable laptops. A fulfillment designer needs to ensure that selected specifications (for example, RAM, SSD) from the commercial laptop product are correctly transferred to its technical product components during decomposition, for accurate fulfillment.

Which mechanism should the fulfillment designer use to transfer the technical product components?
optionA: Quote Line Mapping
optionB: Field & Attributes Mapping
optionC: Decomposition Execution Rules
explanation:

When the commercial laptop decomposes, its technical components are enriched with the mapped RAM and SSD values.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Quote Line Mapping) — not a construct used at decomposition time.
Option C (Decomposition Execution Rules) — decide which technical products a commercial product produces and under what conditions; they do not carry attribute values across. The mapping is defined on the rule, but it is a separate configuration.

question:
After activating an order for a usage-based analytics subscription, a billing specialist wants to confirm that the system has generated the necessary components to support usage tracking, entitlement enforcement, and billing readiness.

Which set of records is created automatically as part of the usage management process?
optionA: Asset, Entitlement Policy, Wallet
optionB: Product Consumption Summary, Rate Adjustment Entry, Billing Event
optionC: Usage Entitlement Account, Usage Entitlement Bucket, Wallet
explanation:
Usage Entitlement Account, Usage Entitlement Bucket and Wallet are the records created automatically. Usage Management creates the entitlement records when the order is assetized. Consumption Management Records lists them: a Usage Entitlement Account "is a customer instance of the purchased product. Usage Management creates this record after an order is assetized" and holds the billing-cycle details; a Usage Entitlement Bucket "represents a wallet that records the credits and debits of a usage resource"; and a Transaction Usage Entitlement stores how grants are tracked, including the rollover and refresh policies and the drawdown order. Those are the components that support usage tracking, entitlement enforcement and billing readiness.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Asset, Entitlement Policy, Wallet) — an asset is created by assetization, but Entitlement Policy is not a Usage Management record, and the wallet is the entitlement bucket rather than a standalone object.
Option B (Product Consumption Summary, Rate Adjustment Entry, Billing Event) — these arise later, as usage is ingested, aggregated and rated — not at activation.

question:
A product bundle has defined a constraint model that is currently in use and has been actively sold for the last few months. A new product will be launched next month and will be sold as part of the same bundle. The product designer updated the bundle structure under Product Catalog Management to add the new product.

What must the product designer do to ensure that the child product is added to the constraint model within the product bundle?
optionA: Use the Visual Builder to add the child product to the constraint model, then import the associations for the type from Product Catalog Management.
optionB: Once a bundle is updated in Product Catalog Management, create a constraint model, then import the associations from Product Catalog Management.
optionC: Create a new type for the child product in the Constraint Modeling Language (CML) Editor, then import the associations for the type from Product Catalog Management.
explanation:
Creating a new type for the child product in the CML Editor, then importing the associations for the type from Product Catalog Management, is what the designer must do. Sync Constraint Models with Product Definitions lists what the Sync button does carry across from PCM — cardinality changes, deleted components, attribute and attribute-value changes — and what it does not, and "Newly added components or attributes" are explicitly on the does-not-sync list. So the designer opens the constraint model in the CML Editor, selects New Type for the child product (choosing the bundle as its parent type), and then creates the association: "Associations are required in constraint models. Create an association to connect a type with a product record", either by importing the relationship from the reference library and product or by adding a type association to the product in the catalog.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (add the child product in the Visual Builder) — the Visual Builder edits constraints and rules with point-and-click tools; types and their associations are created in the CML Editor.
Option B (create a new constraint model) — the bundle already has an active constraint model in use; creating a second model is not how an existing one is extended.

question:

question:
A sales rep is beginning the process of renewing a customer's expired assets in Revenue Cloud.

What is the first step the sales rep should take?
optionA: Override Renewal Term using the Managed Assets Component on the Account/Contract record.
optionB: Update the Asset's Lifecycle End Date on the Current Asset State Period and Asset Action records.

The renewal start falls on or after the lifecycle end date, and if there is a gap the system adds a zero-quantity asset state period to cover it.

A Salesforce Consultant duplicated the amend, renew, and cancel Salesforce flow to customize it, allowing users to attach an existing Opportunity when clicking “Amend”, “Renew”, or “Cancel” on the Manage Asset Viewer. The new flow has been activated, but when users click any of the buttons, the original behavior still occurs.

optionA: The consultant did not select the new flow in the Manage Asset Viewer component in the Lightning Record page.
optionB: The consultant did not update the managing assets flow under Revenue Settings to point to the new flow.

A Revenue Cloud Consultant wants to customize the Transaction Line Editor to display an existing custom field, Estimated Delivery Date, for sales reps when they are working on Quote record pages.

What is the correct method to achieve this customization?
optionA: Add Estimated Delivery Date as a selected field to the Transaction Line Editor component in the Quote Lightning Record page.
optionB: Enable ‘Instant Pricing’ under Revenue Settings to automatically display all custom fields on the Transaction Line Editor.
optionC: Add the Estimated Delivery Date field to the relevant Quote Line Item page layout to display the field in the Transaction Line Editor.

One caveat from the same article: "If you add custom fields to the Transaction Line Editor or Sales Transaction Line Editor columns, add those fields to the context definition used for sales transactions. Otherwise, changes made to those fields in the editor aren't saved."

question:
A product designer is setting up a product bundle that consists of T-shirts and caps. They want to ensure customers can order a maximum of three T-shirts and three caps, but the total number of products should not exceed five.

How should the product designer set this up?
optionA:
*Define the local cardinality for T-shirts with a minimum quantity of three and a maximum quantity of three. 
*Define the local cardinality for caps with a minimum quantity of three and a maximum quantity of three.
*Define a product group that contains both of these products, and set the group cardinality with a minimum quantity of one and a maximum quantity of six.
optionB:
*Define the local cardinality for T-shirts with a minimum quantity of one and a maximum quantity of three. 
*Define the local cardinality for caps with a minimum quantity of one and a maximum quantity of three.
*Define a product group that contains both of these products, and set the group cardinality with a minimum quantity of one and a maximum quantity of five.
optionC: Define the local cardinality for T-shirts with a minimum quantity of one and a maximum quantity of three.
explanation:
Local cardinality of one to three on each of T-shirts and caps, with a product group containing both and a group cardinality of one to five, is the setup. Two different limits are in play, and Revenue Cloud expresses them with two different constructs: local cardinality sets the default, minimum, and maximum quantity allowed for an individual component, and group cardinality constrains the group the two components sit in, which is how the overall ceiling of five is imposed — without it, three plus three would allow six.
One caveat: the documentation describes group cardinality as the minimum and maximum number of child components users can add, which is a count of components rather than a sum of their quantities. Option B is the intended and best-supported answer, but read the group limit as the documented component count.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (min and max of three on each, group max of six) — forces exactly three of each rather than allowing up to three, and sets a group maximum of six, the number the requirement explicitly rules out.
Option C (local cardinality on T-shirts only) — omits caps and the group entirely, so neither the cap limit nor the combined limit exists.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.product_catalog_local_cardinality_and_group_cardinality.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer B stands and is clearly the intended answer, but flagged with a precision caveat: Salesforce documents group cardinality as constraining the number of child components, not the total of their quantities, so 'total number of products should not exceed five' maps onto it only loosely.

question:
A customer reaches out to the Billing Operations of a company requesting to change their monthly billing date. Their current billing date is the 15th of each month, but the customer would like it changed to the 20th of each month. On the forthcoming cycle, the customer has also requested to move the billing date to April 22 for this month only.

Which steps should Billing Operations take to meet this request?
optionA: The Billing Operations user should select the Billing Schedule Group(s) (BSG) for that asset, and change the parameters on the transaction to the 20th for Billing Day of Month and to the 22nd of April for Override Next Billing Date by doing an inline edit.
optionB: The Billing Operations user should process an Amendment canceling the existing Asset and creating a new Asset with the start date of 20th, and then update the Billing Schedule Group’s Override Next Billing Date to 22nd April.
optionC: The Billing Operations user should process a change order with Period Boundary Day on the Order Item as 20th and update the Override Next Billing Date on the Billing Schedule Group to 22nd of April by doing an inline edit.
explanation:
Selecting the Billing Schedule Group for the asset and inline-editing Billing Day of Month to the 20th and Override Next Billing Date to April 22 is what Billing Operations should do. Both changes are field updates on the Billing Schedule Group, made directly on the record. Salesforce documents Update Billing Schedule Groups as "Update billing schedule group fields at any time. You can update the billing day of month, next billing date override, billing and shipping addresses, tax treatment, and the payment term", with the procedure being to open the record, update the fields, and save. Bill Day of Month is "the day of the month on which a recurring billing process is scheduled to occur", so setting it to 20 moves the recurring date; when the billing type is Advance the next billing and charge dates realign after the first invoice, producing one partial-period invoice. Next Billing Date Override "overrides the next billing dates of all the billing schedules" and "is used only once for generating invoices. It's removed after the invoices are generated", which is exactly a one-time move to April 22 for this month only. It must be later than today and fall between the effective next billing date and the group's end date.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (an amendment cancelling the asset and creating a new one) — a commercial change to what the customer owns, not a billing-date change; it would generate cancellation and new billing schedules rather than reschedule the existing ones.
Option C (a change order with Period Boundary Day on the order item) — Period Boundary Day is a field on the order product that defines how billing periods are segmented, set through the order, not through a change order raised to move an invoice date. The documented control for the invoice day is Bill Day of Month on the billing schedule group, edited in place.

https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.blng_advance_and_arrears.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ind.billing_schedule_group_update.htm&language=en_US&type=5

Update Billing Schedule Groups documents Bill Day of Month and Next Billing Date Override as fields updated directly on the Billing Schedule Group record, which is option A. question:
A Revenue Cloud Consultant wants to automatically sync the family field (Family) from the Product2 object to the Quote Line custom field (Family__c) during quoting.

How should the consultant address this using only Revenue Cloud functionality?
optionA: Create an Apex trigger on the quote line item to query the information from the Product2 'Family' field and write it back to the Quote Line.
optionB: Update the Product Discovery Context by mapping the Catalog Product and the Product2 nodes and then mapping the Family and Family__c fields.

optionB: Adding the Flow Name in the Product Discovery Setup.

question:
Universal Containers (UC) sells its products and services to other businesses, and provides an automatic discount to businesses that buy in bulk. UC is now expanding its selling channels and plans to sell directly to end users. A key requirement is to ensure that bulk discounts are only applicable to businesses and not individual buyers.
How should the Revenue Cloud Consultant solve this requirement?
optionA: By using Quote Transaction Type and Volume-Based Pricing
optionB: By using Sales Transaction Type and Volume-Based Pricing
optionC: By using Order Transaction Type and Volume-Based Pricing

For example, B2B customers receive volume discounts while B2C customers see standard pricing." You create a Sales Transaction Type record that names the pricing procedure, add a custom field to the quote or order for reps to flag the transaction, and a record-triggered flow stamps the Sales Transaction Type ID onto the transaction so pricing runs the matching procedure; only the business procedure includes the Volume Discount element.

question:
A customer currently owns subscription products with a term of 3 years. A ramped deal was configured to sell the products with a quantity of 20 in year one, 30 in year two, and 40 in year three. The list price of the product is US$1,000 per year. The subscription started on June 24, 2025, and will end on June 23, 2028. Today’s date is January 15, 2026.

What is the formula to calculate the current Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR)?
explanation:
MRR = (20 x $1000) / 12 is the formula for the current monthly recurring revenue. MRR is a rate, so it reflects what the customer is contracted to pay right now — not the whole deal spread thin. On January 15, 2026 the subscription is inside its first ramp year, which runs from June 24, 2025, and that year carries a quantity of 20 at US$1,000 per year; the current annual value is 20 x $1,000, and dividing by the twelve months of that year gives the current MRR. This is also why an asset state period is defined as a span holding a constant quantity, amount, and MRR: each ramp year is its own period with its own MRR, and the current one is what MRR means.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B ((20 x $1000) / 36) — spreads one year's revenue over the entire three-year term, understating the current rate.
Option C (sum of all three years / 36) — the average MRR across the whole deal, a different and lower figure than the rate in force today; by construction it would never equal the MRR of any individual ramp year.

question: A sales user created a quote with one line item last week, and new features were deployed to production over the weekend. This week, the sales user observed several issues while configuring the quote: The Browse Catalog is not showing products, and configuring any of the existing line items is showing the error “Something went wrong while processing your configuration changes.” What is a reason for the issues?
optionA: The context definition for the pricing procedure must use the context definition selected on the Revenue Settings page.
optionB: The context definition for the pricing procedure must use the context definition selected on the Product Discovery Settings page.
optionC: The context definition for the pricing procedure must use the context definition selected on the Pricing Setup page.
explanation:
The pricing procedure's context definition having to match the one selected on the Product Discovery Settings page is the reason. Product Discovery and the pricing procedure it calls must share a context definition: Configure Product Discovery Settings carries the rule as an Important note — "The qualification procedure and pricing procedure for Product Discovery must use the context definition selected on the Product Discovery Settings page." A weekend deployment that changed the pricing procedure's context definition without updating Product Discovery Settings leaves Browse Catalog unable to hydrate products and the configurator failing on existing lines — the two symptoms reported.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the context definition selected on Revenue Settings) — Revenue Settings registers flows and feature toggles; it does not select the context definition used by Product Discovery.
Option C (the context definition selected on Pricing Setup) — Salesforce Pricing Setup selects the default pricing procedure, not a context definition that Product Discovery must match.

question:
A Revenue Cloud Consultant is configuring a product catalog in Salesforce Revenue Cloud for an electronics manufacturer. The team requires real-time product filtering during the quote process, based on customer tier, location, and purchase history. The consultant needs to use a context definition to pass the required data to the qualification rule.

Which configuration correctly uses a context definition for this customer?
optionA: Configure a Product Discovery context definition with nodes and attribute mappings for account tier and location, so this data can be evaluated by the rules during Browse Catalog.
optionB: Create a Sales Transaction context definition to control which products are visible in the catalog based on the user’s profile, leveraging context tags to enforce record visibility.
optionC: Use the Product2 object to create custom fields and assign page layouts that dynamically control product availability using context definition tags and validation rules.
explanation:
Configuring a Product Discovery context definition with nodes and attribute mappings for account tier and location, so the rules can evaluate that data during Browse Catalog, is the correct use of a context definition. Qualification rules run during product discovery and read their inputs from the context Product Discovery hydrates; mapping the account's tier and location onto that context is what lets the rules filter the catalog in real time as the quote is built.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a Sales Transaction context definition with tags enforcing record visibility) — the sales transaction context carries the quote or order for pricing; it is not what Browse Catalog's qualification rules read, and context tags do not enforce record visibility.
Option C (custom fields on Product2 with page layouts and validation rules) — page layouts and validation rules govern record editing; they cannot filter what the catalog offers a given customer.

question:
A Revenue Cloud Consultant wants to restrict the ability to cancel subscriptions via the cancel button in the Account > Managed Assets view. The consultant wants to ensure that only a select group of super users has access to this functionality.

Which change does the consultant need to apply for this requirement?
optionA: Inactivate the Amend, Renew, and Cancel Assets screen flow for users who should not have access to the cancel button.
optionB: Unassign InitiateCancellation API permission for users who should not have access to the cancel button.
optionC: Modify the Managed Asset Viewer page layout for users who should not have access to the cancel button.
explanation:
Unassigning the InitiateCancellation API permission from users who should not have the cancel button is the change. The lifecycle actions in the Managed Asset viewer are gated by their own API permission sets: Salesforce documents the parallel case explicitly — renewing assets from the Managed Asset viewer requires the InitiateRenewal API permission set together with Sales Rep persona permissions — and the permission table lists InitiateAmendment API, InitiateCancellation API, and InitiateRenewal API as separate permission sets granting read-write access to Asset Lifecycle objects and APIs. Because they are separate, cancel can be withdrawn without disturbing amend or renew.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (inactivate the Amend, Renew, and Cancel flow for some users) — a flow is active or not for everyone; deactivating it would remove all three actions for all users, not just cancel for some.
Option C (modify the Managed Asset Viewer page layout) — hides a control rather than revoking the ability; a determined user or an API call would still reach the action.

question:
A product administrator notices that the price of a warranty product is not being calculated correctly. It should be calculated as 10% of another equipment products last price, but only when the products are purchased together in the same quote or order. This calculation works correctly for other products, but not for this specific warranty product.

How should the product administrator resolve this issue?
optionA: Find the Derived Price element and add the appropriate input/output variables in the pricing procedure.
optionB: Find the Derived Price record where Product = Warranty and set the Derived Pricing Scope to Transactional.
optionC: Find the price book entry of the equipment product and enable the is Derived checkbox.
explanation:
Finding the Derived Price record where Product = Warranty and setting the Derived Pricing Scope to Transactional resolves the issue. Implement Derived Pricing defines the two dimensions: the Pricing Source says where the price originates (Product, or Header for the whole cart), and the Pricing Scope says how it is calculated — "Transactional: The price is derived from one or more specific products within a transaction"; "Non-transactional: The price is derived from the total cost of all products in the transaction cart"; or Both. A warranty priced at 10% of the equipment product only when both are in the same quote or order is the Transactional scope on the warranty's derived price record.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (add variables to the Derived Price element in the procedure) — the element already works for the other products, so the pricing procedure is not what is wrong; the fault is in this product's derived price configuration.
Option C (an Is Derived checkbox on the price book entry) — no such checkbox exists; derived pricing is configured through derived price records and discovery procedures.

question:
A Revenue Cloud Consultant is helping a customer cancel a portion of their subscription for a product that was purchased multiple times over the past year, each at a different price point. When the cancellation is processed, the refund or credit amount will be based on the purchase price of the product.

Which pricing strategy is being used to determine the cancellation value?
optionA: FIFO (First In, First Out) – Uses the earliest asset’s price to determine the refund or credit.
optionB: Average Cost – The system averages the prices of all purchases to calculate the cancellation value.
optionC: LIFO (Last In, First Out) – Uses the most recent asset’s price to determine the refund or cancellation credit.
explanation:
LIFO — Last In, First Out — is the pricing strategy used to determine the cancellation value. Salesforce states the rule in Cancel Assets with the Managed Asset Viewer: "If a cancellation quote line item contains a negative delta quantity, the system calculates the total price based on prior asset sale prices. For assets consisting of multiple prior sales transactions, the system computes the total price based on a Last In First Out strategy." So when part of a product bought several times at different prices is cancelled, the credit is valued against the most recent purchase first.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (FIFO) — would value the cancelled units at the earliest purchase price; the documented strategy is the reverse.
Option B (Average Cost) — no averaging takes place; each cancelled unit is valued at an actual prior sale price, starting from the latest.

question: When a Ramped Asset is renewed using the InitiateRenew API, what happens to its quote line(s) in a renewal quote?
optionA: A quote line for each ramp segment is created but not ramped.
optionB: The Ramped Quote lines are recreated onto the renewal quote.
optionC: One quote line is created for the Asset, and it is no longer ramped.
explanation:
The ramped quote lines are recreated onto the renewal quote. Salesforce documents renewal quotes of ramped assets as carrying an "auto-generated ramp schedule on Amendment and Renewal Quotes", with the segments recreated as ramped lines that the rep can clone or extend but whose auto-generated dates cannot be changed, and Considerations for Ramp Deals adds that "During the renewal of a ramped asset, the price uplift from the final segment becomes the renewal uplift." A ramped asset is a single consolidated asset whose asset state periods represent the segments, and the renewal re-expresses those segments as ramped quote lines.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a line per segment, not ramped) — the segment lines are ramped, not flattened into unrelated lines.
Option C (one un-ramped line for the asset) — the renewal does not collapse the ramp into one line; the ramp structure is preserved.

question:
When activating an order with a contract attached, the Revenue Cloud sales rep notices that the contract does not have the attached assets.

What caused this to happen?
optionA: The Asset Contract Relationship toggle is not active in the Setup → Revenue Settings → Automatically create Asset Contract Relationship.
optionB: The sales rep did not manually create the Asset Contract Relationship object in order for the Contract to be linked to the Assets.
optionC: The Contract does not have the Revenue Lifecycle Management record attached to it, so the system does not automatically create the Asset Contract Relationship records.
explanation:
The Contract not having the Revenue Lifecycle Management record attached is what caused it — the system does not automatically create Asset Contract Relationship records without it. Automatic asset contract relationships depend on the contract carrying the Revenue Management application usage assignment. Create Asset Contract Relationships states the condition: "If an order is linked to a contract with a Revenue Management application usage assignment, the system automatically creates asset contract relationships. This automation occurs when the Create or Update Asset from Order API or Order Product API runs." A contract created outside Revenue Management, without that assignment, is not recognised, so activation links nothing.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (an Automatically create Asset Contract Relationship toggle in Revenue Settings) — no such toggle exists; the behaviour is driven by the application usage assignment.
Option B (the rep must create the Asset Contract Relationship manually) — manual creation exists for linking assets to contracts after the fact, but it is not required when the contract is a Revenue Management contract — the system creates the records on assetization.

optionA: OmniStudio Admin

explanation:

question:
When selecting products to add to a quote, a sales user updates an attribute represented by a custom field. The user intends to use the selected value in other downstream processes.
Which Mapping Intents should they select when creating the Mapping for the context definition?
optionA: Association
optionB: Hydration
optionC: Persistence
explanation:
Persistence is the Mapping Intent to select. A context mapping's intent says what the mapping is for: Persistence writes the context attribute's value back to the mapped Salesforce field, which is what saves the attribute the user set during product selection onto the quote line so downstream processes can read it.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Association) — links a context node to a record so the node knows which record it represents; it does not save an attribute value.
Option B (Hydration) — reads a field's value into the context so a procedure can use it; it populates the context from the record, the opposite direction from what the user needs.

Which permission is the sales rep missing?

question:
A high-tech company offers cloud storage services and wants to define different rates for API calls based on customers' usage patterns.

How should a consultant set up this requirement?
optionA: Use base card entries.
optionB: Use attribute rate entries.
optionC: Use tier rate entries.
explanation:
Using tier rate entries is how the consultant sets up rates that vary with usage. Pricing API calls at different rates based on consumption volume requires the Rate Management data model: a Tier Rate Card contains tier rate entries, where each entry defines a lower bound, upper bound, and an adjustment (percentage or override) applied to the base rate within that consumption band, so the system automatically applies the correct rate as usage crosses thresholds during rating. The key signal in the question is "different rates based on usage patterns", which in Revenue Cloud terminology points directly to tiered, consumption-based rating.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (base card entries) — define a single flat rate for all usage of a resource; there are no bands or thresholds, so every API call would be priced identically regardless of volume.
Option B (attribute rate entries) — Rate Adjustment By Attribute adjusts pricing based on product characteristics such as region or configuration; they are not consumption-aware and have no concept of usage thresholds or volume bands.

question:
A sales rep creates a quote with a subscription product called 'Monitoring' with a quantity of 25 and a term of 36 months, followed by Order creation, activation, and assetization. 'Monitoring' has associated Product Ramp Segments with Segment Type as Yearly.

How many records will be present for Monitoring for each Asset Action and Asset State Period?
optionA: One Asset Action and three Asset State Periods
optionB: One Asset Action and one Asset State Period
optionC: Three Asset Actions and three Asset State Periods
explanation:
One Asset Action and three Asset State Periods is the count. There is one sale here, so there is one asset action — the initial assetization. The ramp is what multiplies the state periods: with Segment Type set to Yearly across a 36-month term, the subscription passes through three successive yearly segments, and because an asset state period is the span over which quantity, amount, and monthly recurring revenue stay constant, each segment is its own period.
This is worth holding onto because it qualifies the usual rule. Normally an asset has as many state periods as it has changes, since each amendment adds one of each. A ramp breaks that one-to-one relationship: the periods are created up front from the ramp schedule rather than by separate transactions, so periods can outnumber actions without anything having been amended.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (one Asset Action and one Asset State Period) — ignores the ramp; three yearly segments produce three periods.
Option C (three Asset Actions and three Asset State Periods) — counts each segment as a transaction, but there was only one sale, so only one action.

question:
In Salesforce Revenue Cloud, a consultant is setting up a new user who will primarily be responsible for managing customer assets.

What is a fundamental requirement to ensure this user can effectively view and manage customer assets?
optionA: The products must be configured as assetizable, and the createOrUpdateAssetFromOrder flow action should be triggered.
optionB: The user must have the Customize Application permission enabled on their profile to view the Assets on Accounts.
optionC: The Asset viewer must have a Salesforce CPQ Plus license assigned to access the Asset-related objects.
explanation:
Products configured as assetizable, with the createOrUpdateAssetFromOrder flow action triggered, is the fundamental requirement. There is nothing to manage until assets exist, and in Revenue Management assets come from activated orders through the Create or Update Asset from Order action. Automate Asset Creation from Orders describes the standard setup: a record-triggered flow on Order, firing when Status becomes Activated, checks for the Revenue Lifecycle Management application usage assignment and invokes Create or Update Asset from Order. The products themselves must be assetizable for the action to produce assets. Once the assets exist, the user views and manages them in the Managed Asset Viewer with the asset lifecycle permission sets.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Customize Application on the profile) — a setup permission for administrators; not what lets a user see assets on accounts.
Option C (a Salesforce CPQ Plus license) — a different product's license; Revenue Management asset access comes from its own permission sets.

question:
A customer would like to begin implementing Revenue Cloud to better manage their company's selling, fulfilling, and financial processing.

Which strategy should the company use for a successful Revenue Cloud implementation?
optionA: Assemble a team with expertise in Quote-to-Cash processes, create a phased plan covering core setup, and scoping for activities such as data migration and customization.
optionB: Prioritize the setup of developer tools like IDX Workbench and Postman, and focus primarily on custom Apex and Lightning Web Component development to meet unique business needs.
optionC: Immediately enable all Revenue Settings, create all user profiles, and assign all recommended permission sets to the System Administrator to accelerate the technical configuration.
explanation:
Assembling a team with Quote-to-Cash expertise, creating a phased plan covering core setup, and scoping data migration and customization is the strategy. Revenue Cloud spans selling, fulfilling and financial processing, so the implementation needs people who understand the end-to-end process, a phased plan that gets the core catalog, pricing and transaction setup right before layering on the rest, and explicit scope for migration and customisation — the two areas that most often blow up an implementation when left implicit.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (prioritise developer tools and custom Apex/LWC) — puts custom code before process design and configuration; most of Revenue Cloud is declarative, and code-first is how implementations become unmaintainable.
Option C (enable every Revenue Setting and grant every permission set to the admin) — enables features nobody has designed for and hands the administrator permissions the business has not decided anyone needs.

question:
A user reports they are unable to see the Managed Asset Viewer on Account record pages. A Revenue Cloud Consultant investigates and confirms that the Managed Asset Viewer component has not been added to the Account record page.

How should the consultant ensure that users can view and edit asset data using the Managed Asset Viewer?
optionA: In Lightning App Builder, drag the Managed Asset Viewer to the Account record page. Select the checkbox to show the side panel when a user clicks a record link.
optionB: Assign the user a permission set that grants Read access to Account record pages and Read access to Assets. Next, drag it onto the Account page layout.
optionC: Verify that the user has the Revenue Lifecycle Management license. Then, enable the Assets-related list on the Account record page to show the Managed Asset Viewer.
explanation:
Dragging the Managed Asset Viewer onto the Account record page in the Lightning App Builder, and selecting the checkbox to show the side panel when a user clicks a record link, is how the consultant fixes it. The Managed Asset Viewer is a Lightning App Builder component: Add the Managed Asset Viewer Page Layouts gives the steps in the option's own words — ensure the Assets related list is on the page layout, then "Go to Lightning Record Pages, select your page layout, and click Edit to open the Lightning App Builder. Drag the Related Lists component and the Managed Asset Viewer component on the layout. Select the checkbox to show the side panel when a user clicks a record link." Users then expand bundles and edit asset data in the viewer or its side panel.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a permission set, then drag onto the page layout) — a permission set grants access but places nothing on the page, and components are added in the Lightning App Builder, not on the page layout.
Option C (verify the license, enable the Assets related list) — enabling the related list shows the standard related list, not the Managed Asset Viewer; the component must be added.

question:
A product's attributes are organized across the attribute categories Tech Specs and Utilization, except for two of the attributes, which are not assigned to any attribute categories. This product is added as a component of a bundle product.

In what order will the attribute categories be displayed when the product configurator is launched for the bundle?
optionA: Attribute categories are randomly displayed and can vary by the instances of product configurator launched
optionB: Attribute categories are displayed based on the sequence defined on the attribute category records, with Uncategorized displayed at the end
optionC: Attribute categories are displayed in alphabetical order, with Uncategorized displayed at the end
explanation:
Attribute categories are displayed in the sequence defined on the attribute category records, with Uncategorized at the end. Reorder Attribute Categories and Attributes says so directly: "Attribute categories and their attributes appear to reps in the order that you set. Reorder them to match your business process rather than relying on the default alphabetical order." From the product or classification's Attributes tab, Reorder Attribute Categories lets you drag categories into sequence, and the attributes without a category "appear in the Uncategorized section" and are ordered individually because they carry no category sequence.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (random, varying between launches) — the order is deterministic and administrator-controlled, never random.
Option C (alphabetical, Uncategorized at the end) — alphabetical is only the default before an administrator sets a sequence; once set, the sequence governs.

question:
A customer is delinquent on their payments.

How should a Revenue Cloud Consultant stop invoicing the customer’s account?
optionA: Assign themselves the Billing Administrator permission set, navigate to Scheduled Jobs, and delete the invoice scheduler’s scheduled jobs.
optionB: Assign themselves the Billing Operations User permission set, go to the customer’s account, and delete their related pending invoices.
optionC: Assign themselves the Billing Administrator permission set, go to the customer’s account, and use the Suspend Billing button.
explanation:
Assigning the Billing Administrator permission set, opening the customer's account, and using the Suspend Billing button is how to stop invoicing the account. Suspend Billing is a quick action on the Account (and on a Billing Schedule Group). Manage Suspend and Resume Billing documents it: open the Account record, click Suspend Billing from the quick actions menu, specify the suspension date and a resumption date, and click Suspend; "no invoices are generated for the account or billing schedule group between the suspension date and the day before the resumption date." The action is available to the Billing Admin, Billing Operations User or Billing Customer Service User permission sets, and it is reversible — Resume Billing updates the resumption date or cancels the suspension. Suspending defers the charges rather than waiving them, so once the account is current, billing resumes and the deferred period can be invoiced or credited.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (delete the invoice scheduler's scheduled jobs) — stops invoicing for every account the scheduler covers, not just this one, and removes the schedule the org depends on.
Option B (delete the account's pending invoices) — discards billing records rather than preventing new ones; the next invoice run would generate them again.

question:
A streaming service company is implementing Revenue Cloud. The company strives to provide fast, reliable, and high-quality streaming services. It’s running a promotion for new customers for a 100% discount on the first month of service. Also, streaming costs go up every year, and the company would like to be transparent about this with its customers during the sales cycle, as its minimum contract length is 36 months.

How should the Revenue Cloud Consultant meet this requirement?
optionA: Enable Ramp Deals. Configure Product Ramp Segment with Segment Type of Free Trial and Monthly. Associate both of these segment types to the product.
optionB: Enable Ramp Deals. Configure Product Ramp Segment with Segment Type of Free Trial and Yearly. Associate both of these segment types to the product.
optionC: Enable Ramp Deals. Configure Product Ramp Segment with Segment Type of Free Trial and Custom. Associate both of these segment types to the product.
explanation:
Enabling Ramp Deals and configuring Product Ramp Segments with Segment Types of Free Trial and Yearly is how the consultant meets the requirement. A product ramp segment carries one of three documented segment types: Free Trial, Yearly, or Custom. Create a Product Ramp Segment spells out each — "To try the product at no additional cost for a specified duration, under Segment Type select Free Trial, enter a trial duration, and select the duration type"; "To create a segment for a specific number of years, select Yearly"; "To create a segment for a custom duration, select Custom" — and adds that "To associate a trial segment at no additional cost with a product, first associate a yearly or custom segment with that product." The free first month is therefore a Free Trial segment, and the price rising once a year across a 36-month minimum term is three Yearly segments, each with its own price. Together they show the customer up front how the cost changes over the contract.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Free Trial and Monthly) — Monthly is not a segment type; the three documented types are Free Trial, Yearly and Custom, so there is no way to build this option.
Option C (Free Trial and Custom) — Custom exists for durations that are not whole years; annual increases over a three-year term are exactly regular, so Yearly expresses them directly and Custom would add configuration without adding anything the requirement needs.
